(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 150 South Union Street in Canton, Mississippi, shall be known and designated as the “First Sergeant Landres Cheeks Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “First Sergeant Landres Cheeks Post Office Building”.

fable.w: This section only names a post office building and deems references in federal records to use that name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" in subsection (b) signals rulemaking, but it merely lists types of existing records and grants no authority to issue rules. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only names a Postal Service facility and says that existing references to it should be read as the new name. Its mention of "regulation" is part of a list of records, not an authorization to make rules, so it does not set up rulemaking or a comment period. No outside party is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
opus.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “First Sergeant Landres Cheeks Post Office Building”.
opus.b:
**Step 1 – Analysis.** One could misread the word "regulation" in subsection (b) as a grant of rulemaking authority. It isn't one. The word only appears in a list of documents in which existing references to the facility will be read as references to the new name. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue is created. The section simply names a post office.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates a specific post office building with a commemorative name. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in making this decision. The action is purely legislative and administrative, involving only federal entities.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a building after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision to name the building. It is a unilateral legislative designation.
